parts.note: a machine that is working is on
the two axes of a graph are labelled Y and X

explanation.surface: A mason shaping a gemstone with an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools, but it means the axes of a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a gemstone.

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it, to put up with it
split as A plus way, and a way is a road, abbreviated RD

explanation.surface: Someone tells a bear to take its flag and go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' must be split into 'a' and 'way'; RD, short for road, stands for the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or flag carried as an emblem, as by a regiment.

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service
provided that means the same as if

explanation.surface: A church service is laid on in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming a distinct upland block.

indicators.note: convulsions throw the letters of made nark into violent disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating a poisonous plant gave an informer convulsions.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a toxic Mediterranean herb of the nightshade family with a forked root.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: playing a pipe
second meaning

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses look like a description of a sizzling performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping is playing on pipes, and piping hot describes food straight from the oven.

clue.text: In Paris I receive fine for facetious remark

parts.note: the French word for I is je
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A visitor to Paris is fined for making a flippant comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as a penalty paid in Paris, but it means all right.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke is a remark made in fun, which is what facetious means.

clue.text: Opening letter, I nail it up the wall

indicators.note: going up the wall means going crazy, so the letters of I nail it go wild

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pins the first letter of a sign up on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the wall' looks like a place to nail something; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a word or name, the one that opens it.

clue.text: Caretaker to retire initially after New Year

indicators.note: after places these letters behind the New Year piece

parts.note: January 1st, written JAN I, is the start of a new year
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of retire

parts.note: the opening letter of retire is taken

explanation.surface: A caretaker plans to retire in the new year.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Year is JAN I, the first of January, not just JAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building, cleaning and maintaining it as a caretaker does.

clue.text: A little fox engages much bigger animals

indicators.note: a little of the phrase means only a part of its letters is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small fox takes on far larger beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little fox' reads as a small fox, but 'A little' points to a part of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle, far larger than a fox.

definitions.meaning: reads as a grammatical category such as noun or verb, but means a short extract from a speech
flags that the familiar phrase is taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: Grammar's parts of speech are a false trail; this part is a snippet clipped from what someone said.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundbite is a short quotable extract from a speech or interview, broadcast on its own.

definitions.meaning: read the clothing word as two parts: a prefix meaning too little, and a verb for having clothes on
signals the playful split of the word

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two parts, under plus wear, meaning to wear something too seldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is clothing worn beneath outer garments, such as pants and vests.

clue.text: Squad heartily taking two females for drink

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes on the next one
the heart of squad is its middle letters

parts.note: squad without its outer letters, leaving its heart
F twice, the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A sports squad drinks heartily with two women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' looks like describing how they drink, but it asks for the heart of squad.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaff is to drink deeply and with gusto.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the strongest piece in chess
second meaning: the British band of Freddie Mercury

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess queen moves any distance in any direction, and Queen were a famous British rock group.

definitions.meaning: seems to mean at present, but refers to air currents
how a room feels when a cold current of air blows through it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' looks like 'just now' but is about currents of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughty room has cold air blowing through it, which makes it chilly and unpleasant.

indicators.note: endless cuts off the final letter

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: The London police are a subject that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Boy holding end of the leash

indicators.note: holding means the lad has the other letter inside him

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word the

parts.note: the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A boy grips the end of a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is the British word for a dog's leash.

clue.text: Thorny plant becomes coated, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a kettle furs, or furs up, when it becomes coated with scale

explanation.surface: A thorny plant gets a coating of something.
explanation.walkthrough: To fur is to become coated, as a kettle does with limescale.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze is gorse, a spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heathland.

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of of desert come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling a desert tree-covered would be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a wooded landscape is the wrong way to describe a desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Forested means covered with trees, the opposite of a barren desert.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group working together, as on a ship
second meaning: past tense of crow, to exult over a victory

explanation.walkthrough: 'triumphed' suggests winning, but the word is the old past tense of crow, to gloat.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a working team, and crew is an older past form of the verb crow, to boast.

definitions.meaning: the ordinary meaning: dim, without a clue
this puzzle has plenty of clues, so it is the opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer literally as without clues, which a crossword never is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clueless is ignorant or dim, having no idea what is going on.

clue.text: Moving here soon, such a tiny town

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; a tiny town is a one-horse town

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters of here soon around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family moving soon to a very small town.
explanation.definitionFit: One-horse describes a small, dull, backward place, as in a one-horse town.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cheer of congratulation
second meaning: a ... Henry is a loud upper-class young man

explanation.walkthrough: A Hooray Henry is a British term for a brash, rich young man, so the word goes before Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooray is a shout of approval, and it is the first part of the phrase Hooray Henry.

clue.text: Colourful sort of light in West

indicators.note: in puts the light inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star
UV, ultraviolet, is a kind of light

explanation.surface: A colourful light shines in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: West is not a direction but the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauve is a pale purple colour, so the clue's adjective stands for this hue.

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the mark, the old German currency
an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A dye plant leaves stains on a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder is a plant whose roots yield a red dye.

clue.text: Do press on, struggling in such a walk?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the walk

indicators.note: struggling makes the letters of do press on writhe into new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone struggling on a charity walk to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsored walk raises money for charity, each mile backed by pledges from sponsors.

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church

explanation.surface: Raising the subject of a small seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, which is what bring up means here.

clue.text: An office may have this property

definitions.meaning: suggests a quality of an office
property here is belongings

explanation.walkthrough: 'property' reads as a quality, but means items handed in, as at a lost property office.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost property is the British name for items found and kept until claimed by their owners.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pass over, omit
second meaning: short for skipper, a captain

explanation.walkthrough: 'the captain' looks like the object of ignore, but it is a second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to leave it out, and skip is an informal name for a team or ship's captain.

clue.text: Hippie: bet on one losing head

indicators.note: on places the bet after the shortened one
losing its head drops the first letter of one

parts.note: the word one, before it loses its first letter
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: A hippie places a bet on a single loser.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Ager follows alternative spirituality, much as the hippies of the sixties did.

definitions.meaning: a pirouette is a spin on one leg
moves the idea to cricket, where a spinner bowls a type of delivery

explanation.walkthrough: Leg spin is a style of slow bowling in cricket; the dancer's spin on one leg gives the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is wrist-spin bowling that turns the ball from the batter's leg side toward the off side.
